slides.title: Name it to *slow it down*
slides.sub: What a UCLA brain-scan study saw when people put feelings into words.

slides.title: What they did
slides.body: 30 people in an MRI scanner looked at faces showing emotion. Sometimes they picked a word for the feeling, like "angry." Sometimes they just picked a name.

slides.title: What they saw
slides.body: Naming the feeling went with less activity in the amygdala, a part of the brain tied to emotional reactions. Picking a name didn't.

slides.title: Keep it in proportion
slides.body: The lead researcher said the effect is likely modest. It's a brake, not an off switch. (Lieberman et al., Psychological Science, 2007)

slides.title: Try it today
slides.body: When something hits hard, finish this sentence, even silently: "Right now I feel ___." Pick the most exact word you can.
